subject: terraforming

resources.title: NASA Astrobiology
resources.notes: Use as evidence base for habitability and life-support research, not as proof that planetary-scale terraforming is currently feasible.

resources.title: Planetary Data System Atmospheres Node
resources.notes: Planetary atmosphere observations and mission data.

resources.title: Planetary Data System Geosciences Node
resources.notes: Planetary geology, geochemistry and surface science data.

resources.title: Environmental Control and Life Support Systems
resources.notes: Real spacecraft life-support engineering reference; applicable to habitats, not planetary-scale environmental modification.

resources.title: Life Support Subsystems
resources.notes: NASA JSC reference covering research, analysis, development and testing of open- and closed-loop life-support technologies including atmosphere revitalization, oxygen generation, contaminant control and water recovery. This supports habitat engineering, not claims of planetary terraforming feasibility.

resources.title: Next Generation Life Support (NGLS)
resources.notes: Archived NASA program documenting bioregenerative closed-loop life support and ISRU concepts including crop production, water recovery from Mars regolith, atmospheric oxygen/methane production and dust challenges. Historical technology evidence only; maturity and current applicability must be verified separately.

resources.title: Advanced Plant Habitat
resources.notes: Active ISS plant-growth research facility providing real evidence for controlled-environment plant biology and closed-loop plant support; it does not demonstrate a self-sustaining planetary biosphere.

resources.title: Building Earth-like Planets: From Nebular Gas to Ocean Worlds
resources.notes: Graduate planetary-science curriculum covering differentiation, crust formation, atmospheric degassing, surface-water condensation, volatiles, terrestrial planets, habitability and biosignatures. Provides scientific prerequisites for evaluating habitable environments, not a terraforming recipe.

resources.title: Extrasolar Planets: Physics and Detection Techniques
resources.notes: Quantitative course on exoplanet characterization, temperatures, composition, biosignatures and habitable conditions using real data. Mapped only to the scientific habitability/environment cells relevant to the existing taxonomy.

resources.title: Atmosphere, Ocean and Climate Dynamics
resources.notes: Assessed physics curriculum on atmospheric and ocean circulation and climate-controlling processes. It supplies climate-system fundamentals only; it is not evidence that planetary climate can be deliberately controlled at scale.

resources.title: Ecology I: The Earth System
resources.notes: Assessed ecology curriculum with problem sets, exams and projects covering energy/material flows, hydrologic/carbon/nitrogen cycles, ecosystem structure and population interactions. Supports biosphere and closed-loop ecology fundamentals without implying engineered planetary biosphere feasibility.

resources.title: The Solar System
resources.notes: Undergraduate planetary-science course with homework and exams covering planetary formation, interiors, surfaces, atmospheres, life in the Solar System and Mars exploration. Radiation mapping is limited to general space/planetary-environment context rather than shielding engineering.

resources.title: Space Radiation
resources.notes: Current NASA evidence on ionizing-radiation exposure, risk characterization, models and countermeasure research for exploration beyond Earth's protective atmosphere. This supports radiation-environment and settlement-risk knowledge, not a complete radiation-shielding curriculum.

resources.title: In-Situ Resource Utilization
resources.notes: NASA capability reference for resource acquisition and processing, including regolith simulants and Mars-atmosphere oxygen production. Mapped to local resource utilization and habitat support, not planetary-scale terraforming.

resources.title: Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment (MOXIE)
resources.notes: Mars flight demonstration that electrochemically produced oxygen from atmospheric carbon dioxide. Evidence for local ISRU oxygen production only; scaling to settlement needs requires further engineering and it does not demonstrate atmospheric terraforming.

coverage_notes: Terraforming remains a speculative umbrella subject; mappings represent established enabling sciences and engineering rather than proof that planetary-scale terraforming is feasible.

NASA life-support, plant-habitat, radiation, ISRU and MOXIE materials strengthen habitat, biosphere, water, regolith, atmosphere and settlement evidence while preserving technology-maturity and scale caveats.
MIT planetary-science, climate-dynamics and ecology courses strengthen assessed instruction using only exact existing taxonomy keys.

Foundation-level coverage remains intentionally sparse because the available authoritative sources are generally introductory college, engineering or research materials rather than purpose-built foundation curricula.

Validated planetary-scale atmospheric modification, climate intervention, self-sustaining artificial biospheres and full radiation-shielding engineering remain genuine gaps; speculative proposals must not be counted as demonstrated capability.
Research references, archives, technology demonstrations and courses do not establish ATLAS expert readiness without runtime retrieval, practical verification, assessment and provenance checks.
